Plot the components of an edge mixture model

Source: R/bison_mixture.R
plot_mixture.Rd

Shows the distribution of posterior median edge weights (on the natural scale) as a histogram, with each edge coloured by the component it most probably belongs to. The posterior median and credible interval of each component's mean are shown as a vertical line and shaded band. Use it to see how well the components separate the edge weights.

Usage

plot_mixture(object, num_components = NULL, ci = 0.9, breaks = 30)

Arguments

object

A bison_mixture object from bison_mixture().

num_components

Number of components to show. Defaults to the number with the highest posterior probability.

ci

Width of the credible interval for the component means.

breaks

Number of histogram bins (passed to graphics::hist()).

Value

The data used for the plot, invisibly: a data frame with each dyad, its posterior median edge weight and its most probable component.

See also

bison_mixture(), get_component_means()

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model_mixture(
  "count", num_components = 2, component_weights = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "count_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("count_conjugate")
)
fit_mixture <- bison_mixture(fit_edge, num_components = 3, verbose = FALSE)
plot_mixture(fit_mixture)
